text:
Amy Chen: heads up — hit a weird regen OOM on a few Dedicated nodes during a streaming coldstart. looks like chunk ordering drifted between the safety buffer and the loader.
Raj Patel: ugh. can you paste a short trace / logs? is it safetensors sharded checkpoint?
Amy Chen: yes safetensors. sharded into 64 stripes. warmup path used stream-first (range requests) and then attempted to coalesce into a single mapped buffer. error: 'mmap: invalid offset' followed by KV cache failures.
Jeffrey Lin: suspicious — we recently changed the stripe-alignment for gzipped bundles. if range offsets aren't aligned to the compressed chunk boundaries, the stream assembler can reorder arrival times and our verifier expects strict chunk sequence.
Sylvia Gomez: did the loader fall back to index-first? i.e., check header -> manifest -> map?
Amy Chen: no fallback. runtime chose stream path because manifest was missing in the tar layer (we rely on sidecar manifest for fast starts). warmup-bot then reported partial hydration.
warmup-bot: warmup: model xyz - 42% chunks hydrated, 8 failed chunks, 0 fallback attempts.
Raj Patel: proposal: make the stream assembler emit an ordered-chunk-set token up-front. then loaders treat assembly as idempotent: if assembled order != token -> fail fast and switch to index-first. reduces silent mismatch.
Jeffrey Lin: that could work. small nit: generation pressure means we might lose throughput if we always verify strict order. maybe only enforce token-check for cross-node aggregation (when multiple shard-streams interleave).
Sylvia Gomez: also need to handle compressed bundles. current range requests operate on byte ranges, but gzip means byte offsets are not equivalent to logical chunk boundaries. we should prefer storing a small 'stripe header index' in the object metadata for compressed artifacts.
Amy Chen: agree. short-term patch: when manifest absent, attach a shallow header probe step that reads the first 16KB of each stripe to validate magic + chunk-loc hints. then decide stream vs index-first.
Raj Patel: pseudocode idea:
```
if not manifest:
  probe_headers(stripes) -> header_tokens
  if header_tokens consistent with stripe_index_schema:
    proceed_stream_with_token(header_tokens)
  else:
    fallback_index_first()
```
Jeffrey Lin: +1. we'll also need telemetry fields: header_token_hash, assembly_mismatch_count, fallback_reason. add to warmup-bot payload.
Amy Chen: i'll ship a spike with the shallow probe and token comparison. target: 2-week spike, measure mismatch rate and perf cost.
Sylvia Gomez: think about backpressure: if stream path stalls because of one slow stripe, other shards shouldn't block the coalescer forever. set a small per-stripe timeout and a soft-quorum to proceed (e.g., 90% of stripes) and fetch missing chunks via index-first.
Raj Patel: good point. soft-quorum reduces tail latency while keeping correctness for most workloads. we document the safety tradeoff (possible short-lived degradation for missing chunks, but fallback recovers).
Amy Chen: ok thanks. i'll open a follow-up RFC with: ordered-token format, header-probe contract, telemetry fields, and the soft-quorum timeouts. cc @Jeffrey @Sylvia if you want to review before RFC.
Jeffrey Lin: will review. handoff to infra for S3 metadata to store stripe header index (if we go compressed).
Sylvia Gomez: i'll mock some failure cases and add tests for the token mismatch fallback.
warmup-bot: scheduled job created: warmup-token-probe-spike (runs nightly)
Amy Chen: thanks all — closing this thread for now, will post RFC link when ready. :thumbsup:
